title: Overfitting: regularisation, dropout, early stopping and augmentation

videos.script: Give a network three hundred thousand weights and a hundred pictures, and it will learn the pictures. {{memorise}} Not the digits in them. The pictures themselves, one by one, until it gets every training image right. {{train}} On images it has never seen, it stays about ninety percent right, and grows more sure of its mistakes every epoch. {{val}} That is overfitting, and this lesson builds it on purpose, so there is something to cure. {{cures}} The first cure makes large weights cost something. It is called weight decay. {{decay}} The second switches off half the units at random while training. That is dropout. {{dropout}} The third watches the validation loss, and keeps the weights from its best epoch. {{early}} The fourth makes new pictures, by moving each digit one pixel in four directions. {{shift}} Each one is measured against the same run, and against a run where only the seed changed. {{control}} Alone, most of them move the numbers less than chance does. Together, they move them four times as far. {{table}} And the strongest cure of all turns out to be the one this lesson cannot use. More real data. {{end}}
